realtime_memories.content: blender-agent-mcp: production two-part system in this repo. blender_extension/ is a Blender 4.2+ extension running a loopback TCP bridge (JSON lines, 127.0.0.1:9876, BLENDER_AGENT_PORT env override); mcp_server/ is a stdio MCP server relaying to it. 197 bridge commands across 12 handler domains, 203 MCP tools across 13 modules. Target: macOS, Blender 5.2.0 LTS at /Applications/Blender.app. Plus an Agent Skill at skills/blender-agent-mcp/ (SKILL.md + 6 references, ~7.5k lines); references/_tool_inventory.json is GENERATED by skills/blender-agent-mcp/scripts/gen_tool_inventory.py (make skill-inventory) and is the source of truth — tests/test_skill_docs.py fails on doc drift, so regenerate after adding any tool.

Core working rule for this repo: NEVER trust memory for Blender or MCP APIs — verify live before writing code. Use `Blender --background --factory-startup --python-expr` with get_rna_type() (which raises for missing operators; hasattr on bpy.ops lies because it resolves lazily). All verified findings are recorded in docs/BLENDER_5X_API_NOTES.md; `make probe` re-checks every documented assumption and exits non-zero when one breaks.

MCP SDK 2.0 gotchas that cost time: `mcp.server.fastmcp` was REMOVED — the FastMCP-style class is `MCPServer` from mcp.server.mcpserver (with Image, Context). Tool.inputSchema was renamed to Tool.input_schema. Returning a list like [str, Image] from a tool yields TextContent + ImageContent blocks. CRITICAL: an f-string cannot be a docstring — `f"""..."""` leaves __doc__ as None and ships MCP tools with empty descriptions.

Blender 5.2 API traps found the hard way: sculpt-session operators (mask fills/filters, face sets, mesh filters) SEGFAULT under --background, so they are guarded before invoking; Brush.sculpt_tool is gone (brushes are assets via brush.asset_activate, compound names like 'Inflate/Deflate'); Action.fcurves is gone (slotted actions: action.layers[].strips[].channelbags[].fcurves); unified_paint_settings moved onto each paint mode; geonodes modifier inputs are modifier.properties.inputs[socket_identifier] and modifier.keys() segfaults; manifest permission reasons cap at 64 chars.

Environment + how to run (CORRECTED 2026-08-08 — supersedes the earlier 'uv run hang' explanation). The blender-agent MCP server was failing to load for a different reason: ~/Documents is under iCloud Desktop & Documents sync, and the sync agent sets macOS UF_HIDDEN on files inside the venv, including .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_editable_impl_blender_agent_mcp.pth. CPython 3.12's site.addpackage SILENTLY SKIPS hidden .pth files, so the editable install never put mcp_server/src on sys.path and import blender_agent_mcp raised ModuleNotFoundError. `chflags nohidden` does NOT stick (flag returns in minutes); the stray '... 2.pth' / 'blender-agent-mcp 2' files are sync-conflict artifacts from the same cause. FIXED in ~/.claude.json (backup ~/.claude.json.bak-20260808-093955): command mcp_server/.venv/bin/python, args ['-m','blender_agent_mcp.server'], env PYTHONPATH=mcp_server/src — PYTHONPATH bypasses .pth so it survives re-hiding. Verified: initialize 0.64s, 203 tools, 0 empty descriptions. Any venv reinstall re-breaks this — reach for PYTHONPATH, not chflags. `uv run` separately does hang on env resolution; prefer .venv/bin/python. Fallback if the server is down: drive the bridge directly on 127.0.0.1:9876, one JSON object per line {id, cmd, params}, cmds domain-qualified (objects.create_primitive) except core ones (get_scene_info, render_frame, execute_python). GOTCHA: the bridge reads its main-thread deadline from a reserved `_timeout` key inside params; a plain `timeout` key is just handler data, so without it calls cap at 10s+5s and long renders die with 'timed out after 15s waiting for Blender's main thread'. Verification: `make test` (56 pytest), tests/headless_smoke.py, `make probe`, `make build-ext`.

Known defects + agent-experience feedback delivered 2026-08-08 (first real use of the server to build an asset). CONFIRMED BUGS, both spawned as tasks: (1) shading.set_node_prop crashes on an integer socket index — handlers/shading.py:141 calls bl_rna.properties.get(prop) before the _socket fallback that handles ints — so ShaderNodeMix RGBA sockets (indices 6/7) are unreachable; workaround is legacy ShaderNodeMixRGB plus parking Math constants on socket 0. Fix first: one line, and it is the difference between the shading API working and not. (2) render_frame rejects engine='CYCLES' — handlers/core.py:362 reads the dynamic engine enum off bpy.types.RenderSettings instead of the instance — even with Cycles enabled and already the scene engine. Also observed: render_frame returned a fully transparent frame (alpha 0) reported as SUCCESS at 1800x1150/96 Cycles samples while 1400x900/48 was fine. PRIORITISED IMPROVEMENTS given to the user: (a) reject unknown params instead of silently falling back to the active object — the object-id param is not uniform (mesh.* uses `name`, uv./shading./modifiers.* use `object`) and a wrong key silently operates on the wrong thing; highest value, cheap; (b) add look_at to add_camera or a frame_object() helper — there is no viewport orbit tool, so aiming a camera is the only way to see a chosen angle, and every agent re-derives rx=acos(-dz/|d|), rz=atan2(-dx,dy); (c) batch node-graph building (27 nodes/35 links = ~60 round trips) and let callers pass stable node ids, since auto-names like Math.007 force an external key->name map that is lost if a build script crashes; (d) expose per-object ray visibility (visible_shadow etc.) — emissive geometry inside a light blocks it and today needs execute_python; (e) add set_light/set_camera, since add_* creates but nothing edits afterwards. Smaller: document `_timeout`, validate render buffers are non-empty, add curve/arc primitives (no curve support meant the lamp harp is 7 straight cylinders). Praise worth preserving: the actionable error messages, verification-grade returns (dimensions/counts/requested_name vs name), applied+missing_sockets, the linked:true warning, and SKILL.md step 0 are the standout strengths — do not let anyone simplify them away. Open gap: no compositing module (scene.node_tree unexposed).

How the user works on 3D tasks (learned 2026-08-08 lamp build): they want materials authored from scratch — asked for 'your own realistic fabric texture', so build the procedural node graph rather than reaching for a stock/noise shortcut. They judge physical plausibility, not just looks: caught that the lampshade had nothing holding it up. They co-drive the scene live while work is in progress (moved the preview camera mid-session, switched the engine to Cycles) — respect their camera and render settings, do not move them back, and re-read scene state instead of assuming it is where you left it.
